title: Trader short-talk
goal: Decode short words like IPO, EPS, ATH and FOMO.

objectives.text: Decode IPO, CEO, EPS and P/E.
Decode GDP, CPI, Fed and FOMC.
Decode ATH, ATL, EOD, bid, ask, volume and market cap.
Decode DD, HODL, FOMO and YOLO.

slides.text: Traders use short words to save time. You will see them on charts and in the news.
slides.title: Short words

slides.text: An IPO is when a company first sells its stock to people. The CEO is the boss of a company.
slides.title: Company words

slides.text: EPS is the profit a company made for each share. P/E is the price you pay for $1 of profit.
slides.title: Profit words

slides.text: GDP shows how much a country makes in a year. CPI shows how fast prices are rising.
slides.title: Country words

slides.text: The Fed is the bank of the US. It helps set the cost of loans. The FOMC is a team in the Fed that votes on loan costs.
slides.title: The Fed

slides.text: ATH is the highest price a stock has hit. ATL is the lowest price a stock has hit. EOD means the end of the day.
slides.title: Price words

slides.text: The bid is the top price a buyer will pay. The ask is the low price a seller wants.
slides.title: Bid and ask

slides.text: Volume, or vol, is how many shares were bought and sold. Market cap, or mcap, is the price of one share times all the shares.
slides.title: Size words

slides.text: After-hours, or AH, is the time after the stock market closes. Pre-market is the time before trading starts. OTC stocks trade away from the big exchanges.
slides.title: Time and place words

slides.text: DD means you read up on a stock first. HODL means you keep a stock and do not sell.
slides.title: Slang

slides.text: FOMO is the fear of missing out. YOLO is when you bet lots of money on one stock. Both can make people lose money.
slides.title: More slang

slides.text: Some short words name chart tools. You will learn them in Unit 2.
slides.title: Chart words
